purpose: Full-corpus test of OCR-assisted import (text-range trimming + physical fold recovery) on the complete proofread set @312–@333 (21 pages; @329 does not exist in the book scan set — dataset numbering jumps 328→330). Two probes preceded this on @333 alone.

method.corpus: 21 proofread .gj pages vs PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 results (one batch run, 22 images fetched, 22/22 succeeded, service-local, most deduped from prior probes)
method.range: per page: normalized difflib alignment of full OCR text vs full proofread text; micro CER, coverage, first/last-10-char anchor presence
method.folds: OCR markdown blank-line groups as physical lines; proofread line-end offsets mapped into OCR coordinates via matching blocks, snapped to nearest group boundary, scored at ±0/±2
method.trim_replay: ocr_trim_continuation replayed for the 4 continuation boundaries (330→331…333→334); retroactive replay is confounded for pages whose earlier pages were later re-proofread — noted per boundary

range.anchor_note: head10/tail10 substring anchors fail on 9 pages purely due to OCR char errors inside the anchor window (CER there ~5–12%); anchors are diagnostic only, the trim gate already uses region coverage instead

trim_replay.330to331: candidate 281 → trimmed 249; vs proofread continuation 368 — retroactive replay confounded: @330 was re-proofread (space normalization commit) after the boundary was drawn; algorithm cut inside the true remainder
trim_replay.331to332: candidate 827 → trimmed 680 vs 371 — @332's host boundary was re-trimmed by user after import; candidate chain no longer matches placed text
trim_replay.332to333: candidate 456 → trimmed 373 vs proofread 372 — CLEAN replay, +1 char, head&tail identical
trim_replay.333to334: candidate 83, judged fully on-page ('no trim') — correct: @334's proofread opens with exactly those 83 chars before new heads

conclusions: fold recovery generalizes: 384/399 boundaries ±0 (96.2%), 388/399 within ±2 (97.2%); misses are on pages where OCR over-splits groups (blank-line grouping is not perfectly stable: e.g. @331 19 lines → 30 groups) — over-splitting ADDS boundaries, so snapping still finds the true ones; the 11 misses cluster where OCR char errors shift the mapped offset >2

range recognition is reliable corpus-wide (micro CER 5.65%, worst page @328 12.6% — the circled/ligature-heavy final page of 一部) — adequate for trimming since the gate needs only region coverage, not exact anchors

the two retroactively-confounded trim replays are a workflow artifact (earlier pages re-proofread after the next page was imported), not an algorithm failure; the clean chain (@333) and the on-page judgment (@334) both exact

production notes: fold pass must merge OCR over-split groups (join adjacent groups when a proofread band boundary is closer than the group boundary); band-vs-fold discrimination stays with the transcription source
